subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@fintechcorp.com
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alice - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Inference costs have grown ~3x over the past 9 months and are now the single biggest line item for your NLU product.
- Peak-hour latency spikes cause timeouts for some real-time flows (p95 occasionally > 400ms).
- Current infra is fragmented across EC2/GPU instances with limited batching and no KV-prefix caching.

Current stack details you mentioned:
- In-house PyTorch models served on AWS (G4/G5 instances) via a custom Flask + TorchServe layer.
- Typical batch size today: 1 (no batching at request layer).
- No model quantization in production; CPU fallbacks for small requests.

Success criteria for any POC / evaluation:
- Unit economics: target >=50% reduction in $/1k tokens or clear path to that number with batching + quantization.
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for real-time endpoints (same quality).
- Stability: consistent throughput at your peak request rate with minimal error spikes.

Suggested next steps (what I'll do and what we need from you):
1) You: share a 72-hour sampling of production traffic (request/response latencies, avg tokens per request, RPS by endpoint) + a short infra diagram.
2) Me: provision a small Dedicated POC instance and run a workload replay to measure baseline cost/latency with and without batching/caching/quantization.
3) We'll run two experiments: (a) enable batching + dynamic batching window, (b) test int8 quantized model build (if you're open).
4) Schedule 60-min POC kickoff next week to align on goals and timeline.

Attachments: I'm attaching a draft SOW and a simple infra diagram template to make the procurement path easier (FTC_SOW_template.pdf, infra_diagram.png).

Open questions I flagged on the call:
- How sensitive are you to small model output differences from quantization? Any internal test thresholds?
- Do you have a preferred SLAs/uptime baseline for a Dedicated/managed deployment?

Proposed times for kickoff: Tue 2026-03-17 10:00-11:00 PT, Wed 2026-03-18 09:00-10:00 PT, or Thu 2026-03-19 14:00-15:00 PT.

If any of the above is off, tell me and I'll update. Appreciate the time - looking forward to moving this to a short POC.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0142

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@fintechcorp.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Ben - thanks for the thorough recap and for framing the success criteria. Confirming a few items from our side:

- We can provide a 72-hour sample from last week (will include latencies and token counts).
- Current peak: ~450 RPS across all endpoints; typical request is 18-45 tokens, some batch-style bulk enrichment jobs hit 200-400 tokens.
- We currently don't use KV caching at the serving layer; the team is open to testing.
- Quantization: engineering is open to int8 tests but we need to run our QA evals - output parity tolerance is tight (target >98% semantic parity on our eval set).

Procurement: they've asked for your SOW stub and a rough estimate for a 30-day POC cost so they can scope budget. I've copied procurement on this thread (procurement@fintechcorp.com).

We're available for the Tue 10am slot. I'll drop the traffic sample and infra diagram here by EOD.

Alice
Head of ML Platforms | FinTechCorp
alice.wong@fintechcorp.com

Thanks Alice - great to have that context. Short follow-up items from our side:

- I'll generate a 30-day estimated POC cost (ballpark) and attach it to the SOW.
- Marissa (cc'd) will own the technical kickoff and coordinate engineers for the workload replay.
- Can you confirm a technical contact from your infra/serving team (name + email) so we can route the logs ingest instructions?

For the POC: we'll run two parallel experiments over the same replay window:
A) Baseline: run your model on Redwood with default runtime (no quantization, small batching enabled) to measure p95 cost/latency.
B) Optimized: enable dynamic batching + prefix KV caching and test an int8 quantized build (if you give the go).

If QA is strict on parity, we'll keep the quantized build as opt-in - we'll provide side-by-side outputs for your eval set so you can validate.

Action items assigned:
- Alice: drop traffic sample + infra diagram (EOD today).
- Procurement: looking for POC cost approval once Ben sends estimate.
- Marissa: will follow up to schedule the kickoff and loop in solutions engineers.

Ben
